newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd opposition blames gangs for unsolved murders.
newsitem.headline: Kurd opposition blames gangs for unsolved murders.

text.p: A Kurdish opposition party on Tuesday said thousands of people had been killed by state-sponsored crime gangs at the centre of a scandal over alleged links between the Turkish state and the underworld.

"We can say these gangs have a direct links with mystery killings. This is no longer a hypothesis or a guess, this is a reality acknowledged by officials," Guven Ozata, a senior member of People's Democratic Party (HADEP), told a news conferance.
"The exact figure cannot be confirmed but, according to the Human Rights Association, since the middle of the 1980s around 3,500 people have fallen victim to mystery murders," Ozata said.
Rights groups have often charged that shady rightist groups were involved in unsolved murders of Kurdish activists in the southeast, where the army is fighting rebel Kurds.
A security scandal over the relationship between the state, the police and the underworld errupted last month when a police chief and a fugitive mobster died in the same car.
Also in the car was a government MP who heads a Kurdish militia fighting separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels. He was injured in the accident.
"The struggle with PKK has not been carried out within the law so far. There was an attempt to solve problems via forces outside the traditional state apparatus," Ozata said.

"Mystery killings are still taking place. We are trying to feel hopeful about the Prime Minister's statement," he said, referring to comments by Necmettin Erbakan that such gangs would not be allowed to exist within the state.
Eighteen of Ozata's party colleagues, including HADEP leader Murat Bozlak, are on trial charged with links to the PKK.
Human rights groups have long voiced concern over the methods used by Turkey's security forces in dealing with the seperatist insurgency, amid reports of extrajudicial killings and torture.
More than 21,000 people have died in the 12-year-old armed conflict between security forces and the PKK rebels, fighting for autonomy or independence in the mountaneous southeast of the country.
